info.bio:
The Waterboys es una banda formada en 1983 por Mike Scott. La composición de la misma ha girado siempre en torno a músicos de Escocia e Irlanda. Las sedes de la misma se han alternado entre Dublín, Spiddal, Nueva York y Findhorn. Su música ha pasado desde una mezcla de folk Celta hasta el rock'n'roll, siempre con un estilo múy personal otorgado por el talento de su líder Mike.

Tras diez años de grabar y girar sin interrupción, en 1993 se disolvieron y Mike Scott inició su carrera en solitario.

scenes.name: Nueva psicodelia y big music: Echo & the Bunnymen y U2
scenes.book: Postpunk. Romper todo y empezar de nuevo
scenes.author: Simon Reynolds
scenes.desc: En lugar de descender a lo oscuro, elevarse hacia la luz. Liverpool, que no tuvo punk clásico ni postpunk experimental, quería que la música fuera «una fiesta» (Bill Drummond, Zoo): el club Eric's, las bandas fantasma (The Crucial Three, Big in Japan), Wah! Heat, The Teardrop Explodes de Julian Cope. Echo & the Bunnymen, con el minimalismo aprendido de Television y la voz de Ian McCulloch, graban Crocodiles y Heaven Up Here, respuesta luminosa a Closer, y heredan el público huérfano de Joy Division; Ocean Rain los vuelve estrellas pop. U2, «punk positivo» cristiano y pacifista, guitarra de The Edge como sintetizador, quiere ocupar el lugar de Curtis: War (1983), «Sunday Bloody Sunday» en MTV, The Unforgettable Fire con Eno. Alrededor, la «big music» celta de Simple Minds, The Waterboys, Big Country y la neopsicodelia de The Blue Orchids.

scenes.name: Pop británico de los ochenta
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Junto al synth-pop, otros grupos trabajan la atmósfera y acuñan un estilo apagado y melódico que revisa el concepto de pop: Young Marble Giants y Raincoats (proto lo-fi), Felt, Talk Talk (Spirit Of Eden, pionero del slo-core). El revival pop (Everything But The Girl, Sade, Scritti Politti, Prefab Sprout, Style Council, Simply Red); Escocia (Orange Juice, Josef K, Aztec Camera, Blue Nile, el «anorak pop» de los Vaselines) e Irlanda; en Inglaterra, los Smiths (el antídoto del punk, como los Beatles lo fueron del rock'n'roll), Wedding Present, Woodentops, Primitives, Waterboys, Big Audio Dynamite; Roxette y los Sugarcubes de Björk.

podcast.title: Influence on "On a Friday" (1986)
podcast.body: Waterboys was cited as one of the 80s influences apparent on "On a Friday's" 1986 self-issued five-track cassette. "You too, water boys, psychedelic furs, the Smiths."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Formation and International Lineup
podcast.body: The Waterboys were formed by Scottish musician Mike Scott, who recruited musicians from Scotland, Ireland, Wales, and England. Mike Scott has been the sole constant member of the band since its inception. "They were formed by Scottish musician Mike Scott who brought in musicians from Scotland, Ireland, Wales and England. And he's been the only constant member of the band since they began."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Giving Irish Music Back to the Irish
podcast.body: Mike Scott, a Scottish musician, earned praise for his work on albums like "Fisherman's Blues," with some observers suggesting that he had effectively "gave Irish music back to the Irish." "Songs like that had people saying that Scottish Mike Scott gave Irish music back to the Irish, and it's a great example of late 80s Celtic rock."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Implied Association with The Enclave
podcast.body: The Waterboys are mentioned in the context of The Enclave, a short-lived boutique label that aimed to sign artists of a certain caliber, implying a potential association or a similar musical style the label sought to promote. "And we signed to this other label called the OnClave, which was short lived, which just set up to be really good at head, like balance of bastion, like the water boys."

srcs.episode: Sloan In Their Own Words: Part 1

podcast.title: Mike Scott's Immersion in Irish Culture
podcast.body: For their folk period, Mike Scott moved to the Galway region of Ireland in 1987. This move was intended to allow him to immerse himself more deeply into Irish music and culture. "Mike Scott moved to the Galway region of Ireland in 1987, looking to immerse himself deeper into Irish music and culture."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Musical Evolution
podcast.body: The Waterboys' sound evolved over time, starting with their "Big Music" phase, then transitioning into a more folk-oriented style, and later returning to a rock sound. "The Water Boys sound evolved over the years. The Big Music phase came at the beginning of their career. After that they slid more into a folky thing before leaning rock again."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: The Big Music Concept
podcast.body: Mike Scott's vision for the band was to fuse the traditional folk music of the British Isles with rock. He coined the term "The Big Music" to describe their sound, which he defined as "a mystical celebration of paganism. It's exolding of the basic and primitive divinity that exists in everything," essentially meaning anthemic. "Mike liked to call what the band did The Big Music, which is shorthand for, and this is a quote, a mystical celebration of paganism. It's exolding of the basic and primitive divinity that exists in everything, which I guess is just another way of saying, anthemic."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: First Recordings (1986)
xref.body: The earliest existing recording attributed to the band is a five-track cassette from 1986, which they self-issued at Abingdon. At this point, Johnny Greenwood was not yet a member, but a sax player named Razz Peterson was part of the lineup. The tape prominently featured 80s influences from bands like U2, Waterboys, Psychedelic Furs, and The Smiths, with Tom York handling lead vocals at 17 years old. "The earliest recording that seems to exist is a 1986 cassette that was recorded at Elbington."
